title: Chapter 6: Tripura Economy — Agriculture, Industry and Natural Resources

blocks.content: Tripura is primarily an agrarian economy but is increasingly diversifying into services, natural gas-based industries, and tourism. The state's location — surrounded by Bangladesh — historically created economic isolation. However, improving Bangladesh relations, new rail and road links, and natural gas exploration are transforming the economy. Tripura is a Special Category State and receives substantial central funding.

blocks.content: Agriculture supports approximately 50–55% of Tripura's population. The state has about 2.7 lakh hectares of cultivated land — out of a total geographical area of 10.5 lakh hectares. The rest is forest, hills, and built-up area.

blocks.content: NOTE: Tripura's 'Queen Pineapple' has received a GI (Geographical Indication) tag. It is considered one of the best varieties of pineapple in India — sweet, juicy, and with thin skin. Tripura produces about 1 lakh metric tonnes of pineapples annually and is the third largest pineapple producer in India. The pineapple is sold across NE India and also exported.
6.3 Natural Gas — The 'Gas State of India'

Tripura is one of India's most important natural gas producing states. The state's unique Tripura Fold geology has resulted in significant natural gas reserves. The gas fields are distributed across the state, primarily in the Gomati, West Tripura, and Dhalai districts.

cells: One of the oldest and most productive; gas used for power generation

items: Total estimated natural gas reserves in Tripura: Approximately 400–500 billion cubic feet (BCF) — significant but not as large as Assam or Gujarat
Gas-based power: OTPC (ONGC Tripura Power Company) runs the 726.6 MW Palatana Power Project in Udaipur district — among the largest gas-based power plants in India; supplies power to northeast states
Fertiliser plant: IFFCO uses natural gas from Tripura; major industrial use
Gas bottling: LPG bottling plants use local gas; reduces dependence on imported LPG
Tripura's natural gas contributes to the 'energy security of Northeast India'

blocks.content: Tripura is India's second largest producer of natural rubber (after Kerala), with approximately 90,000 hectares under rubber cultivation. Rubber cultivation was introduced in Tripura systematically in the 1960s and has grown dramatically. The state government, Rubber Board, and farmers have collaborated to develop rubber as a major cash crop.

items: Rubber districts: West Tripura, South Tripura, Gomati, Sepahijala
Rubber varieties: RRII 105, GT 1, PB 260 — high-yielding varieties
Rubber processing: Centrifuged latex, RSS (Ribbed Smoked Sheet) are produced
Rubber Park at Bodhjungnagar (West Tripura): Industrial park for rubber processing and rubber products manufacturing
Tripura receives Rubber Board of India's most productive rubber state award regularly
Climate: Tripura's humid subtropical climate is ideal for rubber trees
